issues.title: Retail has no self-service onboarding/first-user path (any platform)
issues.customer_impact: Total -- a fresh install cannot be used by a real customer at all; no way to create the first login.
issues.financial_impact: Indirect -- blocks all revenue from this product until fixed.
issues.reproduction_steps: 1) Fresh Retail install, empty database. 2) Attempt POST /api/onboarding/create-admin or open Android SetupScreen. 3) Observe 404 (route not registered).
issues.expected_result: A first-run admin account can be created via the API, matching Clinic's behavior.
issues.actual_result: 404 -- onboarding_bp is never imported/registered in products/retail/backend/app.py.
issues.evidence: docs/audit/12-retail-functional-audit.md CRITICAL FINDING section; contrast with products/clinic/backend/app.py lines 56,62.
issues.affected_ui_screens: Android SetupScreen.kt; web onboarding UI if any
issues.test_coverage: None -- no test exercises Retail onboarding via the API (existing tests insert users directly into SQLite)
issues.suspected_root_cause: Extraction oversight -- Clinic correctly wires the shared commercial_runtime.identity.onboarding_routes.onboarding_bp; Retail's app.py never does.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add `from commercial_runtime.identity.onboarding_routes import onboarding_bp` and `app.register_blueprint(onboarding_bp)` to products/retail/backend/app.py, mirroring Clinic exactly.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: End-to-end: fresh DB -> create-admin -> login -> reach dashboard, on both Windows and Android.

issues.title: Android Retail POS omits tax and discount on every sale
issues.customer_impact: Every Android sale under-collects tax and cannot apply a discount -- real revenue/compliance impact on every transaction.
issues.financial_impact: High -- persistent $0 tax_amount/discount_amount on every Android-originated sale regardless of configured tax_rate.
issues.data_integrity_impact: sale_items.tax_rate/discount_pct persisted as 0 for all Android sales, corrupting historical reporting.
issues.security_impact: None directly (see AUDIT-003 for the related server-trust issue)
issues.reproducibility: Always (100%) for any taxable/discounted item sold via Android
issues.reproduction_steps: 1) Configure a product with tax_rate=15 on either platform. 2) Sell it via the Android POS. 3) Compare the persisted sales.tax_amount to the same sale made via Windows POS.
issues.expected_result: tax_amount and discount_amount computed per core/retail/pricing.py's after_discount default, matching Windows.
issues.actual_result: tax_amount=0, discount_amount=0 always; no discount UI exists in the Android cart at all.
issues.test_coverage: None -- zero Android automated tests exist
issues.suspected_root_cause: Android UI was migrated without porting the web frontend's tax/discount _recalc() logic, combined with AUDIT-003's server-side trust gap.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Fix AUDIT-003 first (move computation server-side into create_sale via core/retail/pricing.py); this alone fixes the Android symptom without any Android-side change needed.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Submit a raw API request with only unit_price/qty (no tax_amount/discount_amount) and assert the server computes them correctly regardless of client.

issues.title: create_sale() trusts 100% of client-submitted financial totals with no server-side recomputation
issues.customer_impact: Any client (including a tampered one) can submit an arbitrary total; legitimate clients differ in correctness (Windows correct, Android wrong -- AUDIT-002).
issues.financial_impact: High -- core/retail/pricing.py exists and is correct but is never invoked by the one route that persists a sale.
issues.security_impact: Server-side financial-input-validation gap -- a modified client or direct API call can submit any total.
issues.reproduction_steps: POST /api/sub/retail/sales with subtotal/total set to an arbitrary value inconsistent with the submitted items; observe it persists as-is.
issues.expected_result: Server recomputes subtotal/discount/tax/total from items + product tax_rate via core/retail/pricing.py, ignoring client-submitted aggregates.
issues.actual_result: `subtotal=float(data.get('subtotal',0))` etc. -- direct trust, no recomputation.
issues.test_coverage: None -- no test submits an inconsistent client total to check for server rejection/correction
issues.suspected_root_cause: core/retail/pricing.py was built as a documented 'single source of truth' but never actually wired into the route that needs it.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: In create_sale(), compute subtotal/discount/tax/total server-side via pricing.calculate_line()/calculate_invoice() from items + company tax_calculation_mode + product tax_rate; treat client-submitted aggregates as advisory/ignored.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Extend retail_pricing_test.py Part B to submit a deliberately-wrong client total and assert the persisted sale reflects the server-computed correct one.

issues.title: create_return() has no validation against the original sale (linkage, quantity, or duplicate-submission)
issues.customer_impact: Any user with POS access can repeatedly submit the same return, each time crediting a refund and inflating inventory -- a direct cash-loss/fraud vector.
issues.financial_impact: High -- unlimited, repeatable, self-service refund creation with no approval step.
issues.data_integrity_impact: inventory_balances can be inflated without bound via repeated returns.
issues.security_impact: No authorization/approval control beyond ordinary POS login -- no manager override or second-approval required.
issues.reproduction_steps: 1) Submit a POST /api/sub/retail/returns payload once. 2) Submit the identical payload again. 3) Observe a second, independent refund + inventory credit with no rejection.
issues.expected_result: A return should validate sale_id exists and belongs to the company, that returned quantity doesn't exceed what was sold (net of prior returns), and should be idempotent/duplicate-protected.
issues.actual_result: No sale_id existence check, no quantity-vs-sold check, no duplicate-submission guard of any kind.
issues.affected_ui_screens: RetailExtraScreens.kt returns UI (Android); web returns UI
issues.test_coverage: retail_pricing_test.py covers correctly-formed full/partial/multi-line returns only -- none of the abuse cases above
issues.suspected_root_cause: Route was built to record a return, not to validate one against sale history -- likely an oversight rather than a deliberate design choice, given create_sale has an idempotency_key and this route does not.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Require and validate sale_id (company-scoped existence check); sum prior returns per sale_item and reject a new return that would exceed the originally sold quantity; add an idempotency_key matching create_sale's pattern.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Attempt return-without-sale, over-quantity return, and duplicate-submission cases; assert all three are rejected.

issues.title: Retail discount is not clamped (can exceed subtotal or be negative)
issues.customer_impact: A fat-fingered or malicious discount value (e.g. 150%) produces a negative sale total with no rejection.
issues.financial_impact: Medium -- possible only via unusual input, but nothing prevents it.
issues.data_integrity_impact: None beyond the negative total itself.
issues.reproducibility: Always given the input (100% given a discount_pct > 100 or < 0)
issues.reproduction_steps: Submit discount_pct=150 on a sale line; observe a negative taxable_amount/total with no error.
issues.expected_result: discount_pct/discount_amount clamped to [0, subtotal], matching Clinic's create_invoice().
issues.actual_result: No clamping anywhere in core/retail/pricing.py or the web JS mirror.
issues.affected_ui_screens: POS cart (web + Android, once Android gets discount UI per AUDIT-002's fix)
issues.suspected_root_cause: Clamping was added to Clinic's create_invoice() (commented 'mirroring the POS fix') but never back-ported to Retail's own pricing module.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add the same clamp Clinic uses: discount_pct/discount_amount bounded to [0, 100]/[0, subtotal] in pricing.py.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Unit test discount_pct=150 and discount_pct=-10 both produce a clamped, non-negative result.
issues.dependency_on_other_issue: AUDIT-003 (should be fixed as part of the same server-side-computation change)
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 53911a9; discount clamped via pricing.clamp_discount_pct(); tests: retail_financial_authority_test.py::test_discount_over_100_percent_is_clamped_not_rejected / ::test_negative_discount_is_clamped_to_zero

issues.title: Two different rounding strategies coexist in Retail (round() vs Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP)
issues.customer_impact: Currently dormant (pricing.py isn't invoked by create_sale) -- would produce off-by-one-cent discrepancies at exact half-cent boundaries once AUDIT-003 is fixed, unless fixed together.
issues.financial_impact: Low currently, would become Low-Medium once pricing.py is wired in.
issues.reproduction_steps: Compute a line total that lands exactly on a half-cent via pricing.py's round() vs. _money()'s Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP; compare.
issues.expected_result: One consistent rounding rule across the whole money-handling path.
issues.actual_result: pricing.py uses Python's round() (banker's rounding); retail_api.py's _money() uses Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Two modules written independently without a shared rounding utility.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Have pricing.py use the same Decimal/ROUND_HALF_UP helper as _money(), ideally sharing one function.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Unit test a value landing exactly on a half-cent boundary through both paths, assert equal.
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 53911a9; core/retail/pricing.py rewritten to Decimal + ROUND_HALF_UP; 26/26 retail_pricing_test.py still pass

issues.title: Retail returns don't separately track a tax component (reporting gap)
issues.customer_impact: A tax-liability report netting sales tax against returned tax cannot be built correctly from current data.
issues.financial_impact: Medium -- compliance/reporting risk, not a same-transaction cash error.
issues.data_integrity_impact: returns table has no tax_amount column distinct from refund_amount.
issues.reproduction_steps: Process a return of a taxed sale; inspect the returns row -- no tax component is stored separately.
issues.expected_result: returns should record tax_amount/discount_amount reversed, distinct from the flat refund total.
issues.actual_result: refund = sum(item.line_total) only -- one undifferentiated number.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Returns were modeled after a simpler refund concept before the tax-mode system existed.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add tax_amount/discount_amount columns to returns, populate from the original sale's line data (once AUDIT-004's sale-linkage validation exists to make this possible).
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Return a taxed sale, assert a tax-liability report nets correctly.

issues.title: Negative sale-line quantity is accepted and inflates inventory disguised as a sale
issues.customer_impact: A crafted request with a negative item quantity increases stock while appearing as a sale.
issues.financial_impact: Medium -- combined with AUDIT-003, a negative-quantity line also affects the (already-untrusted) total.
issues.security_impact: Requires only ordinary POS/API access, no special privilege.
issues.reproducibility: Always (100%) given a negative quantity input
issues.reproduction_steps: POST /api/sub/retail/sales with an item quantity of -5; observe inventory_balances increases instead of decreasing.
issues.expected_result: Quantity <= 0 rejected with a 400.
issues.actual_result: `qty = float(item['quantity'])` with no sign check.
issues.affected_ui_screens: N/A (not reachable via the normal UI, direct-API only)
issues.suspected_root_cause: No input validation on item quantity sign.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Reject quantity <= 0 in create_sale's item loop.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: POST a negative-quantity item, assert 400.
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 53911a9; create_sale() rejects non-numeric/<=0 quantity; tests: retail_financial_authority_test.py::test_zero_and_negative_quantity_rejected

issues.title: Server never prevents negative stock in create_sale
issues.customer_impact: Concurrent sales of the last unit, or a direct API call, can drive stock negative, corrupting any valuation/margin report.
issues.financial_impact: Medium -- indirect, via corrupted inventory valuation.
issues.reproducibility: Reliable under a race or a direct oversell API call
issues.reproduction_steps: Sell more of a product than is on hand via a direct API call; observe quantity_on_hand goes negative with no rejection.
issues.expected_result: Sale rejected or flagged if it would drive stock negative (or an explicit backorder concept, if intended).
issues.actual_result: Unconditional `UPDATE inventory_balances SET quantity_on_hand = quantity_on_hand - ?`.
issues.affected_ui_screens: Android's addOne() client-side guard exists but is not a substitute for server enforcement
issues.suspected_root_cause: Client-side-only stock guard, no server-side check.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Check current quantity_on_hand before decrementing; reject or flag oversell server-side.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Two rapid concurrent sales of the last unit; assert only one succeeds.
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 53911a9; BEGIN IMMEDIATE + stock check in create_sale(); tests: retail_financial_authority_test.py::test_insufficient_stock_rejected_and_does_not_touch_inventory

issues.title: Cross-file pytest run causes 38-64 spurious test failures (test-infrastructure defect)
issues.customer_impact: None directly -- this affects developer/CI confidence, not the shipped product.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.reproducibility: Always (100%) when running `pytest products/{retail,clinic}/tests` as a single combined command
issues.reproduction_steps: Run `pytest products/retail/tests -q`; observe 38 failures. Run each file individually; observe 0 failures, 116 total passes.
issues.expected_result: A single `pytest products/retail/tests` command should be a trustworthy regression check.
issues.actual_result: registry_db.py's DB_PATH is a module-level constant frozen at first import, ignoring later test files' AURA_APP_DATA changes.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Module-level path caching combined with Python's import-once module-cache semantics, never designed for multi-file single-process pytest runs.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Make DB_PATH resolution lazy (computed inside get_conn() from the current os.environ value) instead of a module-level constant.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Run the full combined `pytest products/retail/tests products/clinic/tests` and confirm 211/211 pass in one process.
issues.wave0_resolution: Decision: Option B (defer). See docs/corrections/wave0/wave0-residual-risk-register.md -- P3, not release/enterprise blocker, isolated-per-file strategy remains the trusted baseline (263/263 tests pass)

issues.title: Clinic record_payment has no amount validation (negative/zero/overpayment)
issues.customer_impact: A negative or wildly-overpaid amount is accepted and marks the invoice paid with no cap or correction.
issues.financial_impact: High -- payment amounts are financial records with zero server-side sanity checking.
issues.security_impact: None (tenant isolation on this route is correctly enforced -- see AUDIT-012's note)
issues.reproduction_steps: POST /api/sub/clinic/payments with amount=-50 or amount=999999 against a small invoice; observe it's accepted.
issues.expected_result: amount validated as a positive number, capped from meaningfully exceeding the remaining balance (or explicitly tracked as overpayment/credit).
issues.actual_result: `data.get('amount')` inserted directly with no float() coercion, no sign check, no cap.
issues.test_coverage: test_payment_recording_and_invoice_status_transitions exists but doesn't exercise these cases (per source read)
issues.suspected_root_cause: Route focused on the happy path when originally written; validation not added alongside the later IDOR fix.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Validate amount is a positive float; decide and implement an explicit overpayment policy (reject, or track as credit).
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Negative amount rejected; overpayment either rejected or explicitly tracked, not silently absorbed.

issues.title: Clinic record_payment has no idempotency protection (duplicate payment on retry/double-submit)
issues.customer_impact: A network retry or accidental double-tap records the same payment twice, corrupting the invoice's paid/balance status.
issues.financial_impact: High -- 'duplicate payments' is explicitly one of the audit's own P1 example categories.
issues.data_integrity_impact: clinic_payments SUM(amount_paid) double-counts a duplicated submission.
issues.reproducibility: Reliable under a real double-submit (network retry or UI double-tap)
issues.reproduction_steps: Submit the same payment payload twice in quick succession; observe two clinic_payments rows and a doubled SUM.
issues.expected_result: An idempotency-key mechanism, matching create_sale's pattern, collapses a retried submission into one payment.
issues.actual_result: No idempotency_key field or check exists on this route at all.
issues.suspected_root_cause: idempotency_key pattern was added to Retail's create_sale but never propagated to Clinic's payment route.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add an idempotency_key column + check, matching create_sale's implementation exactly.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Submit the same idempotency_key twice, assert only one payment row is created.

issues.title: Clinic invoice creation has no idempotency protection (duplicate invoice on retry/double-submit)
issues.customer_impact: A double-submitted invoice-creation request creates two real, separately-numbered invoices for the same visit.
issues.financial_impact: Medium -- inflates billed totals until manually caught and corrected.
issues.data_integrity_impact: Two clinic_invoices rows for one intended invoice.
issues.reproduction_steps: Submit the same create-invoice payload twice quickly; observe two distinct invoice_number values.
issues.expected_result: Idempotency-key protected, matching create_sale's pattern.
issues.actual_result: `inv_no = f'INV-C-{int(time.time())}-{random.randint(100,999)}'` -- no dedup mechanism.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Same class of gap as AUDIT-012.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add an idempotency_key column + check.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Submit the same idempotency_key twice, assert only one invoice is created.

issues.title: Clinic invoice creation contains a dead, always-failing, silently-swallowed 'mirror into Accounting' call
issues.customer_impact: None to the clinic invoice itself; misleading to a future developer reading the comment.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.reproducibility: Always (100%) -- fails on every single invoice creation
issues.reproduction_steps: Create any invoice; the import `from database.subsystem_db import sub_create, get_accounting_conn` raises ImportError, caught by a bare except.
issues.expected_result: Either the code and comment are removed (Accounting isn't part of this product), or the integration is actually implemented.
issues.actual_result: Import fails silently on every call; the comment claims behavior that cannot occur.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Leftover reference to the original monolith's cross-subsystem integration, not trimmed during extraction.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Remove the dead code block and its misleading comment (Accounting is out of scope for the standalone Clinic product).
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: N/A -- removal only.

issues.title: Clinic invoices have no cancelled/voided/draft state
issues.customer_impact: An invoice created in error has no way to be marked void; only unpaid/partial/paid exist.
issues.financial_impact: Low-Medium -- a real operational annoyance, not a calculation error.
issues.reproduction_steps: Attempt to find a route or status value for cancelling an invoice; none exists.
issues.expected_result: A 'cancelled'/'voided' status and a route to set it.
issues.actual_result: Only 'unpaid'/'partial'/'paid' exist.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Feature not yet built.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add a 'cancelled' status + a route to set it (admin-gated), excluded from revenue reporting.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Cancel an invoice, assert it's excluded from billed-revenue totals.

issues.title: Retail's SQLite connections never enable PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON
issues.customer_impact: Orphan rows (e.g. a sale_item referencing a deleted product) are structurally possible and undetected.
issues.financial_impact: Low-Medium, via corrupted joins in reports.
issues.data_integrity_impact: All declared FOREIGN KEY constraints in Retail's schema are decorative, never enforced.
issues.reproduction_steps: Insert a sale_items row referencing a nonexistent product_id directly; observe SQLite does not reject it.
issues.expected_result: PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON set on every connection, matching Clinic's schema.py exactly.
issues.actual_result: Not set anywhere in Retail's _conn().
issues.test_coverage: None (Clinic has an explicit FK-enforcement test; Retail has no equivalent)
issues.suspected_root_cause: Inconsistency between the two products' otherwise-identical connection-factory pattern.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` to Retail's _conn(), matching Clinic exactly.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Port Clinic's test_foreign_key_enforcement_on_clinic_connection to Retail.
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 57a3048; docs/corrections/wave0/data-integrity-correction.md; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every Retail connection

issues.title: receive_purchase_order has no transaction wrapper or rollback path
issues.customer_impact: A crash partway through receiving a multi-line PO leaves partial inventory increments applied with no complete PO record and no automatic cleanup.
issues.financial_impact: Medium, via corrupted inventory/cost data.
issues.reproducibility: Requires an exception mid-function (e.g. malformed unit_cost) -- not normal-path, but reachable
issues.reproduction_steps: Submit a multi-line PO receipt where one line has a malformed unit_cost; observe earlier lines' inventory increments remain applied with no rollback.
issues.expected_result: Explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION / rollback-on-exception, matching create_sale's pattern.
issues.actual_result: No try/except, no explicit BEGIN, single trailing commit() only.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Route written without the same transactional discipline applied to create_sale.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Wrap in an explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION / try-except-rollback, matching create_sale.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Simulate a mid-loop exception, assert no partial writes remain.

issues.title: Clinic's create_invoice and record_payment have no explicit transaction wrapper
issues.customer_impact: A crash between a payment insert and the invoice-status update can leave a payment recorded with the invoice still showing unpaid/partial -- billed-vs-collected reports would disagree with the sum of actual payments.
issues.financial_impact: Medium-High -- affects the two routes that move money, worse than Retail's equivalent gap in blast radius.
issues.data_integrity_impact: Partial writes possible on exception in either route.
issues.reproducibility: Requires an exception mid-function -- not normal-path, but reachable
issues.reproduction_steps: Simulate an exception between the clinic_payments insert and the clinic_invoices status UPDATE in record_payment; observe no rollback occurs.
issues.expected_result: Explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION / rollback-on-exception on both routes, matching demo_wipe's own pattern in the same file.
issues.actual_result: Neither route wraps its writes in an explicit transaction; only demo_wipe (a rarely-used utility) does.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Same class of gap as AUDIT-017, more severe here given these are money-moving routes.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Wrap both routes in explicit BEGIN TRANSACTION / try-except-rollback.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Simulate a mid-function exception in each route, assert no partial state remains.
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 8f315ab; docs/corrections/wave0/clinic-payment-correction.md; BEGIN IMMEDIATE wraps create_invoice/record_payment; tests: clinic_payment_wave0_test.py::test_invoice_creation_is_atomic_no_header_without_lines

issues.title: No backup or restore capability exists in either product, on either platform
issues.customer_impact: No way to recover data after data loss (device failure, accidental deletion); no way to export/take ownership of data at all.
issues.financial_impact: Catastrophic in the event of data loss (all sales/patient/billing history unrecoverable).
issues.privacy_impact: Medium -- affects patient data recoverability for Clinic specifically.
issues.data_integrity_impact: Total -- no recovery path exists for any data-loss scenario.
issues.reproduction_steps: Search the repo for backup/restore/export-db code; none found. Attempt to find a backup button in either app; the only one found ('Backup & restore' in Settings) opens a 'coming soon' placeholder.
issues.expected_result: At minimum, a manual export-to-file backup and a documented restore procedure.
issues.actual_result: No functional backup/restore code anywhere; a UI element actively implies a feature that doesn't exist.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Feature not yet built.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Build a minimum-viable manual backup (copy/export the SQLite file + WAL/SHM sidecars consistently) and restore procedure before any paid customer relationship.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Take a backup, corrupt/delete the live DB, restore, verify data integrity.
issues.wave0_resolution: commit 4f37e5d, 27dc45b; docs/corrections/wave0/backup-and-restore-foundation.md; tests: retail_backup_restore_test.py (12 passing), clinic_backup_restore_test.py (4 passing)

issues.title: Clinic's GET /patients/<id> has no role gate -- any authenticated role can read full clinical history
issues.customer_impact: A Secretary/front-desk role can read the same clinical visit history a Doctor can, beyond what their job function requires.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.privacy_impact: Medium -- over-broad internal access to sensitive medical data.
issues.security_impact: Authorization design gap (read side, not write side).
issues.reproduction_steps: Log in as a non-doctor role; call GET /api/sub/clinic/patients/<id>; observe full clinic_visits content returned.
issues.expected_result: Clinical content restricted to doctor/admin roles, or a filtered view for other roles.
issues.actual_result: Only @mt_login_required + @mt_require_subsystem('clinic') -- no @require_clinic_role gate on this or any other read route.
issues.test_coverage: None -- clinic_rbac_test.py covers write-side role gating, not this read route
issues.suspected_root_cause: Role model was applied to write routes (where the Phase 3 IDOR review focused) but not extended to read routes.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Decide the intended access policy (e.g. secretary sees demographics/scheduling only, not clinical notes) and either filter the response by role or add a role gate.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Log in as a non-doctor role, assert clinical content is filtered/blocked per the decided policy.

issues.title: Neither Android app sets FLAG_SECURE -- screenshots/recent-apps can capture on-screen data
issues.customer_impact: OS-level screenshot or recent-apps preview can capture on-screen sale/patient data.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.privacy_impact: Medium for Clinic specifically (patient data), Low for Retail.

issues.title: Windows builds are unsigned with no installer wrapper
issues.customer_impact: SmartScreen/Defender warning on first run; no Start Menu entry, no uninstall entry, raw folder distribution only.
issues.financial_impact: None directly, but a real adoption/trust barrier.
issues.security_impact: Low -- unsigned executables are a known, generic AV-flagging risk class.

issues.title: Unparameterized SQL identifier interpolation in Retail's .db/.sqlite import preview (low severity)
issues.customer_impact: None to other tenants/data -- confined to the uploading user's own ephemeral temp-file copy of their own uploaded database.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.reproducibility: Would require a maliciously-crafted table name inside the user's own uploaded .db file
issues.reproduction_steps: Upload a .db file containing a table whose name contains a double-quote character; observe unparameterized f-string SQL construction.
issues.expected_result: Table/column identifiers should be validated or properly quoted, on principle, even though no real exploit path exists.
issues.actual_result: `f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}"'` / `f'SELECT * FROM "{best}" LIMIT 50000'` -- unparameterized identifier interpolation.
issues.affected_database_tables: N/A (a temp-file copy of the user's own upload, not the app's real database)
issues.suspected_root_cause: Table names trusted as safe because they originate from SQLite's own catalog, without considering SQLite's permissive identifier-naming rules.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Validate table names against a strict identifier pattern (e.g. `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`) before interpolating, or use a proper identifier-quoting helper.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Upload a .db with an adversarial table name, assert safe handling.

issues.title: App version numbers are not synchronized across platforms
issues.customer_impact: No single consistent version number a support agent or customer can quote across platforms.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.reproduction_steps: Compare config.py's APP_VERSION to android/*/app/build.gradle's versionName.
issues.expected_result: One synchronized version number across desktop and Android for the same product.
issues.actual_result: 0.1.0 (desktop) vs 1.0.0 (Android), for both products.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Two independently-set version literals, never linked.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Adopt one version source of truth (e.g. a shared VERSION file both build systems read).
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Build both platforms, confirm matching version strings.

issues.title: No index on products.sku/barcode or clinic_patients.name -- future performance risk at real catalog/patient scale
issues.customer_impact: Not observable at small scale (measured fast at 5,000 rows); a real risk at the 50,000+-row scale the product should support for a larger customer.
issues.financial_impact: None directly
issues.reproducibility: Structural (schema-evidenced); not reproduced at true scale in this audit
issues.reproduction_steps: Inspect schema.py for CREATE INDEX statements on products.sku/barcode or clinic_patients.name; none exist.
issues.expected_result: An index on the most frequently point-queried columns (barcode/SKU for POS lookups, patient name for search).
issues.actual_result: No such index in either schema.
issues.source_line: table CREATE statements (no accompanying CREATE INDEX)
issues.suspected_root_cause: Indexes not added as the schema was written; not yet a problem at any scale tested to date.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add `CREATE INDEX idx_products_sku ON products(company_id, sku)` and an equivalent for clinic_patients.name.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Load-test at 50,000+ rows, measure lookup latency before/after the index.

issues.title: Android 'Backup & restore' settings row is a non-functional placeholder that misleads users
issues.customer_impact: A user reasonably believing a backup feature exists (because the UI presents one) has no actual protection.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.reproduction_steps: Open Settings on either Android app, tap 'Backup & restore'; observe a 'coming soon' toast.
issues.expected_result: Either remove the row until the feature exists, or implement it.
issues.actual_result: Row exists, calls a `soon(...)` placeholder helper.
issues.suspected_root_cause: UI scaffolding built ahead of the backend feature (AUDIT-019).
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Remove or clearly label as 'coming soon' with no implication of current functionality, until AUDIT-019 is resolved.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: N/A -- UI copy/visibility change.

issues.title: delete_product's soft-vs-hard-delete branch decision query is not company-scoped (logic gap, not exploitable)
issues.customer_impact: Extremely unlikely in practice (requires a product_id collision across tenants); worst case is choosing the wrong delete branch, not a cross-tenant read/write.
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.data_integrity_impact: Low -- the actual mutating statements are correctly scoped regardless.
issues.security_impact: None (not a live IDOR, per the data-integrity audit's own conclusion)
issues.reproducibility: Only under a cross-tenant product_id numeric collision, which is architecturally possible but not demonstrated as exploitable
issues.reproduction_steps: N/A -- code-review finding, not independently reproduced as an exploit.
issues.expected_result: The existence-check query should also filter by company_id, for defense-in-depth consistency with every other query in the file.
issues.actual_result: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sale_items WHERE product_id=?` has no company_id filter.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Oversight -- every other query in the file consistently filters by company_id.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add `AND company_id=?` to the existence-check query for consistency.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: N/A -- defense-in-depth hardening, not a reproducible exploit test.

issues.title: Per-install secret-key file's chmod call is a no-op on Windows
issues.customer_impact: None beyond the secret file having the same protection as any other file in the user's own profile directory (not weaker than the rest of the app's data, just not additionally hardened).
issues.financial_impact: None
issues.security_impact: Low -- POSIX chmod bits have no effect on Windows NTFS ACLs.
issues.reproduction_steps: Inspect app_secret.py's os.chmod call; note it targets POSIX permission bits with no Windows-specific ACL equivalent.
issues.expected_result: On Windows, an explicit ACL restriction (or an accepted documented no-op) rather than a silently-ineffective POSIX call.
issues.actual_result: `os.chmod(path, stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IWUSR)` wrapped in try/except -- silently does nothing meaningful on Windows.
issues.suspected_root_cause: Code written for a POSIX-first mental model; Windows behavior not specifically considered.
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Document as an accepted limitation, or add a Windows-specific ACL restriction via pywin32/icacls if additional hardening is desired.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: N/A unless a Windows-specific ACL fix is implemented.

issues.title: Both Windows launchers' startup readiness check polls a route no server has ever served, always timing out and killing (or orphaning) a healthy server
issues.customer_impact: Total for the packaged Windows desktop experience -- a real customer double-clicking the shipped exe would, ~45 seconds after a successful start, either see the app killed with a generic error, or (in a non-interactive/no-desktop-session launch context) get a silently orphaned server process with no visible window at all.
issues.financial_impact: None directly (does not corrupt data or misstate money), but blocks all use of the Windows packaged product.
issues.data_integrity_impact: None observed -- the server itself was healthy and the database was never touched by this defect.
issues.security_impact: Secondary finding: the failure path's blocking MessageBoxW call could prevent sys.exit(1) from ever running in a non-interactive launch context, leaving an orphaned, unmanaged server process bound to a loopback port indefinitely.
issues.reproducibility: Always (100%, structural) -- 107/107 (Retail) and 97/97 (Clinic) readiness attempts failed identically in direct reproduction.
issues.reproduction_steps: Launch the packaged AuraRetail.exe/AuraClinic.exe with a throwaway AURA_APP_DATA directory; observe the server start and answer real API requests via an independent curl process within seconds, while the launcher's own internal readiness check (polling bare 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>') fails every single attempt with HTTPError 404 for the full 45s timeout, then calls _fatal().
issues.expected_result: The launcher recognizes its own server as ready within a few seconds and proceeds to open the application window.
issues.actual_result: Every readiness attempt returned HTTP 404 (no route was ever registered for '/'), so the check never succeeded regardless of actual server health; _fatal() then either killed the process or, when its blocking MessageBoxW call could not return (no interactive desktop session), left the process running unmanaged.
issues.affected_api_routes: N/A (fixed by adding GET /api/health to both products' app.py)
issues.affected_ui_screens: The entire desktop application window/launch flow for both products.
issues.test_coverage: None prior to this phase -- no test in the repository exercised either launcher script's main() entry point (all existing tests boot app.py directly via Flask.test_client(), never launcher_retail.py/launcher_clinic.py).
issues.suspected_root_cause: CONFIRMED, not suspected: _wait_for_server(url) was called with url = f'http://{HOST}:{port}' (the bare root path), and neither app.py has ever registered a route for '/' (static_url_path is '/static', not '/'). See root-cause-analysis.md for the full disproof of every alternative hypothesis (proxy, IPv6, threading, port mismatch, race).
issues.recommended_fix_direction: Add a dedicated unauthenticated GET /api/health endpoint and point the readiness check at it; use a monotonic clock and an explicit no-proxy opener; distinguish process-exited/health-endpoint-error/timeout failure reasons; bound the failure dialog so it cannot block process exit indefinitely.
issues.recommended_test_after_fix: Dependency-injected unit tests against the extracted readiness-check logic, plus a real packaged long-run (10+ minute) smoke test proving the server remains reachable well past the old 43-45s failure window and survives a clean shutdown/restart cycle.
issues.dependency_on_other_issue: None (Retail/Clinic launchers are independent of the Wave 0 financial/data-safety fixes; discovered while re-verifying those fixes in the packaged artifact)
issues.phase37_resolution: commits 074ed8b (reproduction), 6a7dbda (fix: /api/health + commercial_runtime/launcher_support.py + explicit LauncherState lifecycle + bounded failure dialog), 47d421a (15 unit tests, all passing); real packaged rebuild + 10+ minute long-run smoke test for both products (docs/corrections/launcher/packaged-long-run-smoke-report.md) -- readiness now achieved in ~2.5s/2 attempts (first launch) and ~1.5s/1 attempt (after restart), both products ran 10+ minutes without incident, clean shutdown with zero orphan processes, full data persistence across restart, PRAGMA integrity_check ok on both databases. Tag windows-launcher-watchdog-corrected.
